title: GrantReady: Australian Government and Queensland business grants
notes: First grant programs for GrantReady: Export Market Development Grants (Austrade), the Industry Growth Program (business.gov.au) and Queensland's Business Growth Fund, from pages read on 2026-10-09. Every reference is UNVERIFIED and carries a summary, not the source's wording: staff must capture each source, replace the extract with the exact text and verify it. Rounds are created with the program and then kept current in the admin screens. None of the three programs was open to applications when read.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] The EMDG program gives grants to Australian small and medium enterprises (and representative bodies) to market and promote goods and services overseas and, at tier 1, for export training. Tier 1 is for businesses ready to export, tier 2 for those exporting within existing markets and tier 3 for those exporting to new key markets. Applications for Round 4 are closed, no round is open now and the timing of the next round has not been confirmed.
references.interpretation: Who EMDG is for and that no round is open. The program is governed by the Export Market Development Grants Act 1997 and the EMDG Rules 2021, which are not encoded. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Tier 1 applicants must not have exported before, have a valid ABN and have traded under the same ABN for at least 2 years, have annual turnover of more than $100,000 but less than $20 million, be able to spend at least $20,000 a financial year of their own money (excluding the grant), match the grant with their own money, complete Austrade-recognised export training or the Export Readiness Test, have a business-specific marketing plan, and be tax compliant. Grants are $20,000 to $30,000 a financial year.
references.interpretation: Tier 1 criteria and amounts for Round 4. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Tier 2 applicants must already be exporting with evidence of recent export sales, have a valid ABN and have traded under the same ABN for at least 2 years, have annual turnover of more than $500,000 but less than $20 million, and be able to spend at least $20,000 a financial year of their own money (excluding the grant), matching the grant. Grants are $20,000 to $50,000 a financial year.
references.interpretation: Tier 2 criteria and amounts for Round 4. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Tier 3 applicants must already be exporting with evidence of recent export sales and be seeking to market in new key markets, have a valid ABN and have traded under the same ABN for at least 2 years, have annual turnover of more than $1 million but less than $20 million, and be able to spend at least $20,000 a financial year of their own money, not other government funding, matching the grant. Grants are $20,000 to $80,000 a financial year, for up to two financial years (2025-26 and 2026-27).
references.interpretation: Tier 3 criteria and amounts for Round 4. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

Tier 1 and tier 3 opened 10am AEDT on 12 November 2024 and closed 5pm AEDT on 20 December 2024. Tier 2 opened 10am AEDT on 12 November 2024 and closed 1:30pm AEDT the same day. references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] To be eligible the applicant must be a company incorporated in Australia, a co-operative or an incorporated trustee applying for a trust; have an ABN, be registered for GST and not be income-tax exempt; have combined annual turnover under $20 million for each of the 3 financial years before applying; and have a project in a National Reconstruction Fund priority area (value-add in resources; value-add in agriculture, forestry and fisheries; transport; medical science; renewables and low emissions technologies; defence capability; enabling capabilities). The product, process or service must be innovative: minor changes or improvements to existing products or services are not. Applicants first receive an Advisory Service and need its report before applying. Early-Stage Commercialisation grants are $50,000 to $250,000; Commercialisation and Growth grants $100,000 to $5 million, as matched funding.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] The Business Growth Fund supports high-growth Queensland small and family businesses to buy specialised equipment that helps them grow, become more productive or efficient, gain market share or expand into export markets. Grants are $50,000 to $75,000 (excluding GST), paid in three milestone payments, and applicants must fund at least 50% of the total project cost. Round 7 stage 2 has closed and recipients have been notified (page last updated 12 June 2026).

rule_sets.title: Export Market Development Grants (Austrade)
rule_sets.description: Eligibility criteria for small and medium enterprises in EMDG tiers 1 to 3, from Austrade's Round 4 criteria pages. Each rule is one criterion and matches when it is met.
limitations: Built from Austrade's Round 4 criteria pages, not the EMDG Act 1997, the EMDG Rules 2021 or the guidelines for a future round, which may change the criteria.
Checks the lowest turnover limit of any tier ($100,000); tiers 2 and 3 need more than $500,000 and $1 million.
Doesn't check export training or the Export Readiness Test (tier 1), the marketing plan, tax compliance, fitness to receive a grant or whether your products are eligible.
Meeting these criteria doesn't mean an application will succeed. Not financial or legal advice: confirm with Austrade or an adviser.
